title: The Drop of the Free Port
premise: Ada Oyelaran, a veteran interpreter for a failing peace delegation, has survived two decades in the diplomatic underworld of the Free Port by being useful, quiet, and forgettable. When a stranger repays a favor she never performed—depositing money, documents, and a debt marked 'with interest'—she realizes someone has been living her life inside the network that trained interpreters like her as deniable assets. As the summit approaches, Ada must trace her double through the Free Port's banks, safehouses, and back channels, discovering the network intends to detonate the peace process and vanish with its architects' fortunes. In the end she burns the network from within during the summit's final session, sacrificing her anonymity forever to expose it—and chooses, for the first time, to be seen.
about_author: Elodie Marchetti is the pen name of a former conference interpreter who spent fifteen years working summits across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to disappear into other people's words.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: Ada Oyelaran, POV. Preparing briefing notes for a doomed summit delegation, Ada receives a courier package: cash, keys, and a note thanking her for a favor she never did, marked 'interest owed.' The emotional beat is cold unease—the first crack in twenty years of careful invisibility.

chapters.title: Rules of the Booth
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Flashback-tinged chapter establishing how the Interpretation Directorate trained her: neutrality, silence, self-erasure. Her mentor Voss's voice still governs her. Beat: nostalgia curdling into suspicion as she recalls how thoroughly the network shaped her.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Meridian Bar
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. She tracks the courier to a dockside bar and meets Tomas Reiner, who insists they met in Geneva in 2009—when Ada was verifiably elsewhere. He describes her, her habits, her tells, perfectly. Beat: vertigo; someone has studied her life like a text.

chapters.title: Delegation of the Doomed
chapters.summary: Ambassador Kessler, POV. The peace delegation's internal fractures: factions bought, briefings leaked, Kessler suspecting his own staff. He notices Ada watching everyone. Beat: paranoia establishes the summit's stakes and the clock ticking toward failure.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The package's bank draft traces to a shell company whose registered director is 'Adaeze Oyelaran'—her own name, with a signature that is almost hers. Beat: dread deepens into obsession; her identity has been counterfeited.

chapters.title: The Archive Under the Custom House
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Following the shell company, she finds a records office where interpreter personnel files are kept—including hers, thicker than it should be, with missions she never ran. Beat: revelation that the Directorate ran a shadow roster.

chapters.title: Voss Returns My Call
chapters.summary: Ada and Voss, alternating. Her old mentor warns her off gently, too knowledgeably. His half of the chapter reveals he knows exactly what's happening and is afraid. Beat: the father-figure revealed as complicit, or trapped.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Was Me
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. He recounts his history with 'Ada': a woman who saved him in Geneva, spoke six languages, vanished owing him. Beat: sympathy for Tomas complicates Ada's anger—her double was good, even kind.

chapters.title: Summit Security Briefing
chapters.summary: Security chief Ilse Brandt, POV. Brandt catalogs threats to the summit and flags an anomaly: an accredited interpreter whose biometrics don't match her file. Beat: the hunter enters the story; the net begins to close on both women.

chapters.title: Ghost Roster
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. She decodes her inflated file: the Directorate trained duplicates of its best interpreters—deniable operatives embedded in delegations, activated for jobs official linguists couldn't touch. Beat: horror reframes her whole career as cover for something darker.

chapters.title: Coffee with a Counterfeit
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Using the file, Ada arranges a meeting and comes face to face with her double—a woman named Mirei who moves like her, pauses like her, and claims she's trying to get out too. Beat: uncanny recognition; enemy and mirror.

chapters.title: What the Network Sells
chapters.summary: Mirei, POV. Mirei explains the business: leaked translations, doctored interpretations that shift negotiations, sold to the highest bidder before each summit. The Free Port summit is the biggest contract ever. Beat: exposition delivered as confession; scale of corruption lands.

chapters.title: Kessler's Doubt
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. A mistranslation nearly collapses a preliminary session; Kessler suspects his interpretation team but trusts Ada instinctively. He asks her quietly to watch the others. Beat: Ada is pulled into the official game she's been avoiding.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada weighs exposure: going to authorities means revealing her own file, her own training, her usefulness to the machine. Beat: the theme crystallizes—survival so far has cost her every claim to a self.

chapters.title: Dead Drop at Pier Nine
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Following Mirei's instructions to a dead drop, Ada finds instead a trap: Brandt's surveillance, and evidence planted framing Ada as the mole. Beat: betrayal; the walls close in and running becomes the only option.

chapters.title: On the Run in the Old Town
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. A tense chase through the Free Port's alleys and fish markets; Tomas shelters her, settling his imagined debt for real. Beat: fear mixed with unexpected warmth—an ally earned by accident.

chapters.title: Brandt Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. Brandt interrogates the delegation's interpreters, dismantles Mirei's cover, and realizes there are two women wearing one life. Beat: antagonist gains dimension—she's honest, and honestly dangerous.

chapters.title: Mirei's Confession
chapters.summary: Mirei, POV. Cornered, Mirei reveals the network's head: Director Voss himself built the ghost roster, and the summit operation will end with delegates dead and the network rich and gone. Beat: the personal betrayal becomes the plot's engine.

chapters.title: The Mentor's Mask
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada confronts Voss privately; he doesn't deny it, offering her a place in the exit plan—her old self-erasure, perfected, forever. Beat: temptation offered in the language of safety; she refuses.

chapters.title: Halfway Point: The Recording
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Midpoint reversal: Mirei gives Ada a recording proving the sabotage plan—but playing it exposes the ghost roster, including Ada. Truth and survival are now the same impossible choice. Beat: stakes fuse; no clean way out.

chapters.title: Allies of Convenience
chapters.summary: Ada, Tomas, and Mirei, rotating. The three fugitives plan how to get the recording into the summit's secure system without triggering Brandt or Voss. Beat: fragile trust forged under pressure; found-family warmth against the dark.

chapters.title: Kessler Learns the Shape of It
chapters.summary: Kessler, POV. Ada risks everything and shows Kessler partial truth. He believes her—not because of evidence, but because he recognizes the exhaustion of a woman used by systems. Beat: alliance with power, purchased with vulnerability.

chapters.title: The Network Fights Back
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Retaliation: Tomas is attacked, Mirei's safehouse burns, and a message arrives in Voss's voice: 'You were trained better than this.' Beat: grief and rage; the cost ledger opens.

chapters.title: Inside the Vault of Voices
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada infiltrates the Directorate's archive to find the operational schedule and learns the detonation point: the closing plenary, when all principals share one room. Beat: grim clarity; the battlefield is chosen.

chapters.title: Brandt's Bargain
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. Brandt catches Ada—and instead of arresting her, offers a deal: give her Voss, and Brandt will bury the ghost roster, Ada's file included. Beat: moral crossroads; the offer of erasure as reward.

chapters.title: The Interpreter's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada realizes accepting Brandt's deal means Mirei takes the fall alone. She refuses the clean version and insists both women's fates be tied together. Beat: integrity chosen at real cost; loyalty over self-preservation.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for Ruin
chapters.summary: Mirei, POV. Mirei infiltrates the summit prep as herself, mapping the plenary chamber's audio systems where the sabotage will run through the interpretation feed. Beat: tension ratchets; the plan takes mechanical shape.

chapters.title: Voss Makes His Offer Public
chapters.summary: Voss, POV. Voss, sensing the net, accelerates the timeline and tests Ada's loyalty with a live assignment: interpret a session in ways that fracture a key alliance. Beat: Ada must perform betrayal convincingly while planning treason.

chapters.title: The Session She Sabotages Perfectly
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada executes Voss's corrupted interpretation flawlessly—and hates how good she is at it. Afterwards she copies the session logs as evidence. Beat: self-loathing and resolve entwined; competence as burden.

chapters.title: Tomas Pays His Debt
chapters.summary: Tomas, POV. Tomas uses his shipping contacts to move the evidence out of the Port ahead of a lockdown, knowing he may not follow it. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed; the favor finally repaid in full.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Brandt, POV. The Free Port seals itself for the summit; communications are cut; the evidence is inside with them now or nowhere. Beat: claustrophobia; all remaining pieces forced onto one board.

chapters.title: The Night Before the Summit
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Quiet chapter: Ada and Mirei rehearse their roles, trade histories, and admit they were made by the same machine. Beat: elegiac calm before the storm; sisterhood across the mirror.

chapters.title: Opening Plenary
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The summit opens; Voss's people are in the booths; Ada interprets flawlessly while tracking the sabotage signal's countdown architecture. Beat: high-wire tension; public performance masking private war.

chapters.title: Mirei Is Taken
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Voss discovers Mirei's betrayal and has her detained in the building's holding rooms—using Ada's own credentials. Beat: gut-punch; her identity weaponized against the person closest to her.

chapters.title: The Booth War
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Climax begins: Ada fights the sabotage in real time, speaking over corrupted feeds, feeding true translations while Voss watches from the gallery. Beat: ferocious concentration; her skill turned into a weapon of truth.

chapters.title: Confrontation in the Gallery
chapters.summary: Ada and Voss, alternating. Above the plenary, Ada confronts Voss; he argues the world runs on men like him and always will. She triggers the broadcast of the recordings through the chamber's own system. Beat: ideological duel resolved by action, not argument.

chapters.title: The Drop of the Free Port
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The recordings play to the assembled delegations; Brandt arrests the network's operators mid-session; Voss, cornered, attempts to destroy the archive and is stopped. Beat: cathartic collapse of the corrupt order in public view.

chapters.title: Aftermath in the Empty Chamber
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The summit salvages a thin, real agreement; Kessler publicly credits an unnamed interpreter. Ada declines anonymity for the first time. Beat: exhausted triumph; the price paid tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Woman
chapters.summary: Ada and Mirei, alternating. Mirei, granted leniency for testimony, chooses exile and a new name freely; Ada keeps hers. They part as equals. Beat: bittersweet resolution of the doubled identity; freedom means choosing your name.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Weeks later, Ada interprets a small open hearing, unmasked, unafraid, her voice simply her own. A letter arrives from Tomas, alive, debt closed. Final beat: quiet transformation—from invisible instrument to visible person; survival redefined as selfhood.
